children: Earnings season continues with 10 companies reporting quarterly results across utilities, industrials, financials, energy, communication services, materials, and information technology.
Out of the 10 companies reporting, all 10 exceeded EPS expectations. Notably, 8 firms posted year-over-year earnings growth (while 1 declined and 1 had no prior-year comparison).
Out of the 10 companies reporting, 8 exceeded revenue expectations, while 2 fell below analyst estimates. Notably, 8 firms posted year-over-year revenue growth.
Let’s take a look at some of the companies that reported earnings this week:

adjusted operating earnings of $5.06 per share, beating the $3.88 consensus estimate, alongside revenue of $9.55B (+45.4% Y/Y). Management raised and narrowed its full-year adjusted operating earnings guidance to $12.50–$12.80 per share, citing Calpine accretion, strong commercial performance, and higher PJM capacity prices.

revenue of $9.03B (+9.5% Y/Y), beating consensus estimates by $310M, while non-GAAP EPS of $3.43 topped forecasts by $0.14. Growth was driven by 7.0% organic expansion and 2.7% from acquisitions, prompting management to raise its calendar 2026 net sales outlook to ~7% growth and narrow its adjusted operating margin target to 9.6%–9.8%.

of $1.78, surpassing the $1.58 consensus estimate, while revenue reached $2.61B (+8.8% Y/Y). Results were bolstered by record fee-related earnings of $1.32B and strong returns in infrastructure (+4%) and alternative credit (+3%), with the firm expecting to return over $40B to clients in 2026.

gained just over 10% alongside a broader utility rally after reporting Q3 revenue of $9.47B (+24.0% Y/Y), beating consensus estimates by $180M, and non-GAAP EPS of $4.68, topping forecasts by $1.65. Management reaffirmed its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $7.90–$9.90 and projected 2027 adjusted EPS of $8.05–$10.05 ($9.05 midpoint).

rose 2.04% post-earnings after reporting better-than-expected Q3 adjusted EPS of $1.91 (beating by $0.44), even as revenue of $6.56B missed consensus estimates. A 32.5% Y/Y jump in average realized oil prices to $85.91/bbl helped offset a 2.5% dip in global production to 1.43M boe/day caused by maintenance and Gulf of Mexico curtailments, with Q4 output guided to 1.43M–1.47M boe/day, with output from the Permian Basin expected to ‌come in at 820K-840K boe/day.

rose 8.31% post-earnings in reaction to its FQ2 results and GTA 6 update, despite total net bookings falling 18% Y/Y to $1.60B (missing the $1.66B estimate) and EPS coming in at $1.00. Looking ahead, the company guided FY27 revenue to $8.0B–$8.2B and EPS to $0.57–$0.75, trailing consensus estimates.

rose 0.55% post-earnings as a soft profit outlook overshadowed a Q4 beat, with revenue rising 22.6% Y/Y to $2.99B (beating by ~$40M) and adjusted EPS of $12.44 topping the $12.21 consensus. While management projected FY27 revenue of $11.95B–$12.15B above estimates, its FY27 adjusted EPS forecast of $47.09–$47.94 fell short of the $48.66 consensus amid higher borrowing costs.

fell 0.06% post-earnings after reporting Q3 revenue of $938M (-0.6% Y/Y), beating consensus estimates by $19.94M, while non-GAAP EPS of -$0.42 topped expectations by $0.10. Supported by continued technology adoption, the company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 outlook for adjusted pro forma operating EBITDA of ~$2.8B and EPS of $2.25–$2.35 vs. consensus of $2.38.

Fueled by strong AI-driven semiconductor demand, the company guided Q1 FY2027 revenue to $10.6B–$11.6B ($11.1B midpoint) and adjusted EPS to $4.15–$4.55 ($4.35 midpoint), both above Street forecasts.
